issues.problem: Paddle publishes explicit limits, so "not published" is incorrect. Most API operations are limited to 240 requests per minute per IP; pricing-preview endpoints allow 1,000 per minute, and additional per-subscription limits apply to immediate-charge updates.
issues.suggestion: Set to "240 requests/minute per IP for most operations; 1,000 requests/minute for pricing-preview endpoints; immediate-charge subscription updates are limited to 20/hour and 100/24 hours per subscription."

issues.problem: "From-Token" is not the PagerDuty header. Certain operations made with an account-level API key require a From header containing a valid PagerDuty user's email address.
issues.suggestion: Replace that sentence with: "For certain requests using an account-level API key, include From: user@example.com. This is generally unnecessary for user-level keys."

issues.problem: The stated 900 requests per minute is outdated. PagerDuty raised the standard REST API limit to 960 requests per minute, with the accounting scope depending on credential type.
issues.suggestion: Use "Generally 960 requests/minute per account API key, per user for user API keys, or per applicable OAuth app/user/account context; endpoint-specific exceptions may apply."

issues.problem: The entry conflates the open-source Pelias geocoder with Geocode Earth's separate hosted commercial service. Pelias itself has no universal hosted base URL, API key, or pricing plan.
issues.suggestion: Rename the entry to "Geocode Earth Geocoding API" and state that the service is powered by Pelias. A separate Pelias entry should describe self-hosting without vendor-specific pricing or authentication.

issues.problem: Geocode Earth's current documentation specifies the api_key query parameter; it does not document an Authorization-header alternative.
issues.suggestion: Use "API key via the api_key query parameter; self-serve signup through Geocode Earth."

issues.problem: Geocode Earth offers a two-week free trial, not a permanent free tier. Paid service currently begins with the Lite plan.
issues.suggestion: Set free_tier to false and describe the no-credit-card two-week trial separately. Current published paid pricing starts at $100/month for 150,000 requests.

issues.problem: Rate limits are published and plan-dependent, so "not published" is incorrect. Current public plans specify per-second limits, while trials also have daily limits and all plans have monthly allowances.
issues.suggestion: State the applicable plan limits, such as up to 10 requests/second on Lite and Basic and 20 requests/second on Advanced, with trial daily and plan monthly limits also applying.

issues.problem: The listed api.goperigon.com hostname is obsolete in current Perigon documentation. The documented API root is api.perigon.io/v1.
The authentication method is already documented and should not be left as needing verification. Perigon accepts apiKey in the query string, Authorization: Bearer, or x-api-key.
issues.suggestion: Use "API key via apiKey query parameter, Authorization: Bearer header, or x-api-key header; header authentication is recommended."

issues.problem: The example uses the obsolete api.goperigon.com hostname rather than Perigon's current documented endpoint.
issues.suggestion: Use "curl 'https://api.perigon.io/v1/articles/all?apiKey=YOUR_API_KEY&q=technology'" or send the key in an Authorization or x-api-key header.

issues.problem: Perplexity publishes detailed, tier-based rate limits, so "not published" is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Describe the current tiered limits. For example, Sonar starts at 50 requests/minute for Tier 0 and scales to 4,000 requests/minute at higher tiers; Sonar Deep Research has lower limits, and the Search API has a separate 50-requests/second limit.

issues.problem: Perspective API is still serving requests in 2026, but it has been formally sunsetted and is scheduled to cease service after 2026. Calling it simply operational omits a material retirement warning.
issues.suggestion: Mark it as "deprecated" or "sunsetting" and note that service ends after 2026.

issues.problem: The claim that users can contact Perspective for higher quotas is no longer current. Perspective stopped accepting new quota-increase requests after February 2026 as part of the shutdown transition.
issues.suggestion: Set paid_plans to null and note that no new quota-increase requests are accepted after February 2026.

issues.problem: Although the stated default 1 QPS limit is plausible, the claim that higher limits remain available through a quota request is outdated.
issues.suggestion: Use "Default 1 QPS for existing access; no new quota-increase requests accepted after February 2026; API scheduled to stop operating after 2026."
